<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">revenue from license fees was 82.7% and 81.5% for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and
2003, respectively. Gross margin on license fees increased primarily due to the
increase in the mix of Lawson products sold versus third-party products, as
Lawson products typically carry higher margins than third-party components.
This is partially offset by the increased amortization of acquired technology,
and by the increase in the mix of embedded third-party products in relation to
total third-party products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cost of Services.</font></i>&#160; Cost of services decreased to $136.3&nbsp;million
for fiscal&nbsp;2004 from $141.7&nbsp;million for fiscal 2003, representing a
decrease of 3.8%. The $5.4&nbsp;million decrease in cost of services was due to
several factors including; a $2.6&nbsp;million decrease in third-party
consulting costs as a result of a lower proportion of third-party services in
our revenue mix, offset by improved third-party margins; a $2.3&nbsp;million
net decrease in expenses due primarily to cost containment initiatives; and a
$1.5&nbsp;million net decrease in employee costs from workforce reductions and
attrition. Partially offsetting these decreases was a $0.5&nbsp;million
increase in transition services and amortization expense related to support
contracts purchased in April&nbsp;2004; and a $0.4&nbsp;million increase in
other third-party maintenance costs primarily due to an overall increase in
maintenance revenues, which is partially reduced by less third-party
maintenance in our revenue mix. Cost of services as a&nbsp;percentage of total
revenues for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and 2003 was 37.5% and 41.1%, respectively. Gross
margin on services revenues was 49.8% and 46.9% for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and 2003,
respectively. Gross margin on services increased primarily due to the increase
in maintenance revenue in proportion to consulting revenue.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Operating Expenses</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Research and Development.</font></i>&#160; Research and development expenses increased
to $64.9&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004 from $59.1&nbsp;million for fiscal
2003, representing an increase of 9.8%. The $5.8&nbsp;million increase in
research and development expenses was due primarily to a $1.8&nbsp;million
increase related to the integration of acquisitions; a $1.1&nbsp;million increase
in corporate initiatives designed to improve future efficiencies and enhance
future functionality; and a $2.3&nbsp;million net increase in employee costs primarily
related to incentives and merit increases. Research and development expenses as
a&nbsp;percentage of total revenues for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and 2003 were 17.8%
and 17.2%, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Sales and Marketing.</font></i>&#160; Sales and marketing expenses decreased to
$93.1&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004 from $103.0&nbsp;million for fiscal
2003, representing a decrease of 9.5%. The $9.9&nbsp;million decrease in sales
and marketing expenses was primarily due to a $5.9&nbsp;million net decrease in
employee costs as a result of our workforce reductions and attrition covering
66 employees; a $5.0&nbsp;million decrease in expenses due to cost containment
initiatives; and a $0.9&nbsp;million decrease in marketing costs. These
decreases were partially offset by a $2.5&nbsp;million increase in corporate
initiative spending intended to enhance product development and emphasize
creation of value for our clients. Sales and marketing expenses as a&nbsp;percentage
of total revenues for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and 2003 were 25.6% and 29.9%,
respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">General and Administrative.</font></i>&#160; General and administrative expenses increased
to $37.7&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004 from $30.0&nbsp;million for fiscal
2003, representing an increase of 25.9%. The $7.7&nbsp;million increase in
general and administrative expenses was primarily due a $2.9&nbsp;million
increase in bad debt expense reflecting an increase in the accounts receivable
reserve for aged receivables; a $2.0&nbsp;million increase in costs related to
corporate initiatives and consulting designed to improve efficiency; a $2.0&nbsp;million
increase relating to the resolution of certain claims and other legal related expenses;
a $0.5&nbsp;million increase in insurance costs, and a $0.4&nbsp;million unfavorable
variability year over year from foreign currency translations. These increases
were partially offset by a $1.3&nbsp;million decrease in employee costs related
to lower stock compensation expense, a $0.9&nbsp;million decrease in expenses
due to a prior year lease termination fee that did not occur in the current
year; and a $0.4&nbsp;million decrease in audit expenses due primarily to prior
year costs related to the Armature acquisition that did not occur again in the
current year. The decrease in stock compensation expense resulted primarily
from decreased amortization of the remaining initial public offering deferred
stock compensation balance and the expiration of unvested options related to
employee terminations resulting from workforce reductions. General and
administrative expenses as a&nbsp;percentage of total revenues or fiscal&nbsp;2004
and 2003 were 10.4% and 8.7%, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restructuring.</font></i>&#160; During fiscal&nbsp;2004, we recorded $2.2&nbsp;million
of restructuring charges, net of reversals, related to corporate restructuring
initiatives.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2003, we approved the fiscal&nbsp;2004 restructuring
plan to realign projected expenses with anticipated lower revenue levels and
incurred restructuring charges of $2.3&nbsp;million for severance and related
benefits. The plan resulted in the termination of 93 employees in the second
quarter of fiscal&nbsp;2004 from various functions including research and
development, general and administrative, and sales and marketing primarily in
the United States. In addition, during fiscal 2004, </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">23</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">we recorded a $0.04&nbsp;million reversal of
costs related to certain employee costs which we determined would not be
incurred for the fiscal 2003 restructuring plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although the fiscal 2003 and 2002 restructuring plans have been fully
executed, we continue to make cash payments for continuing lease and employee
related costs. During the fiscal year ended May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2004, we made
cash payments of $3.1&nbsp;million, which reduced liabilities included in
accrued compensation and benefits and other accrued liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Amortization of Acquired Intangibles.</font></i>&#160; Amortization of acquired intangibles
increased to $1.3&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004 from $0.9&nbsp;million for
fiscal 2003. The $0.4&nbsp;million increase was primarily due to the amortization
of acquired intangible assets other than acquired technology, and the amortization
of service contracts purchased in April&nbsp;2004 which are amortized to cost
of license fees and cost of services, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Other Income
(Expense), net</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other income (expense), net, decreased to $3.2&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004
from $4.5&nbsp;million for fiscal 2003. The reduction in interest income
resulted from a realignment in our investment strategy during the year to
shorter-term lower-yielding investments, and from a reduced investment base
resulting from the funding of acquisitions and stock repurchases.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Provision (Benefit)
for Income Taxes</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognized an income tax provision of $7.3&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004
compared with a tax benefit of $2.4&nbsp;million for fiscal 2003. As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2004,
we recognized a deferred tax valuation allowance of $1.2&nbsp;million that is
included in the current year provision. The valuation allowance is associated
primarily with federal contribution carryforwards, state net operating loss
carryforwards and certain federal tax credit carryforwards not considered
likely to be realized before they expire within the next ten years. Our income
tax provision (benefit) is based on pretax income or loss and consists
primarily of federal and state income taxes. Our effective rate including the
valuation allowance was 47.8% and 39.0% for fiscal&nbsp;2004 and 2003,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005, we had $234.6&nbsp;million in cash, cash
equivalents and marketable securities and $178.4&nbsp;million in working
capital. Our most significant source of operating cash flows is derived from
license fees and services to our clients. Days sales outstanding (&#147;DSO&#148;),
calculated as net receivables at period-end divided by revenue for the quarter,
times 90&nbsp;days in the quarter, was 45 and 59 as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,
and May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2004, respectively. The decrease in the DSO for the three
months ended May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005 as compared with the three months ended May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2004,
was due primarily to a decrease in net receivables as a result of focused
collection efforts. Our primary uses of cash from operating activities are for
employee costs, third-party costs for licenses and services, and facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that cash flows from operations, together with our cash,
cash equivalents and marketable securities, will be sufficient to meet our cash
requirements for working capital, capital expenditures and investments for the
foreseeable future. As part of our business strategy, we may acquire companies
or products from time to time to enhance our product lines.&#160; On June&nbsp;2,&nbsp;2005, we entered into an
agreement to combine with Stockholm, Sweden-based Intentia International
AB.&#160; We intend this to be an all-stock
transaction; however, we may utilize cash to acquire certain shares as well as
to fund </font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">acquisition related costs.&#160; We
believe we have sufficient cash to fund this business transaction.&#160; For additional information, refer to Footnote
18, &#147;Subsequent Events&#148; in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements
as well as the discussion of contingent cash commitments contained below in
this section.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash flows from operating activities:</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net
cash provided by operating activities was $32.9&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2005
compared with $17.8&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004. Our net income of $5.3&nbsp;million
was increased by non-cash charges resulting in $22.9&nbsp;million of cash from
operations before working capital changes. The net working capital changes of $4.7&nbsp;million
increased the overall cash provided to $32.9&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
significant activity in cash flows from working capital changes for fiscal&nbsp;2005
primarily related to a $21.2&nbsp;million increase in cash from trade accounts
receivable, which was partially offset by a $10.2&nbsp;million net decrease in
accrued expenses and other liabilities, and a $6.9&nbsp;million decrease in
deferred revenue and client deposits. The $21.2&nbsp;million increase in cash
from trade accounts receivable was due primarily to focused collection efforts as
well as the effects from a general decrease in revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
$10.2&nbsp;million decrease in accrued expenses and other liabilities was due
primarily to restructuring related cash payments and the payment of fiscal&nbsp;2004
incentive compensation in the first quarter of fiscal&nbsp;2005. Fiscal&nbsp;2005
incentive compensation payments were lower due to partial objectives being met.
The $6.9&nbsp;million decrease in deferred revenue and client deposits was
primarily due to a decrease in cash received on support billings as a result of
a change in client billing cycles. The change in client billing cycles resulted
in initially smaller client invoices due to pro-rata billings in an effort to
get individual multiple client support billings to a common renewal date. The
cash collections generated by the pro-rata billings will fluctuate according to
renewal periods identified by our clients. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net cash provided by operating activities was $17.8&nbsp;million for
fiscal&nbsp;2004 compared with $47.9&nbsp;million for fiscal 2003. Our net
income of $8.0&nbsp;million was increased by non-cash charges resulting in $25.8&nbsp;million
of cash from operations before working capital changes. The net working capital
changes of $16.0&nbsp;million decreased the overall cash provided to $17.8&nbsp;million.
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
significant activity in cash flows from working capital changes for fiscal&nbsp;2004
was due primarily to an $8.2&nbsp;million decrease in cash from trade accounts
receivable, a $3.6&nbsp;million net decrease in accrued expenses and other
liabilities, and a<br>
$6.5&nbsp;million decrease in deferred revenue and client deposits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The $8.2&nbsp;million increase in trade accounts receivable was due
primarily due to $5.7&nbsp;million in products billed with payment terms that
extended beyond the end of the period, and $2.7&nbsp;million from increased
licensing activity. Prepaid expenses decreased $2.3&nbsp;million due primarily
to the reclassification of tax benefits to taxes payable due to annual
earnings. Accrued expenses decreased by $5.4&nbsp;million primarily due to
lower accruals for third-party maintenance services, payment of acquisition
related liabilities, and restructuring related cash payments. Deferred revenue
and client deposits decreased $6.5&nbsp;million due primarily to decreased
maintenance payments received prior to the support period and a decrease in the
sales returns and allowances reserve due to the resolution of certain product
claims.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash flows from investing activities:</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net
cash provided by investing activities was $82.2&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2005
compared with net cash used in investing activities of $27.5&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004.
Cash provided by investing activities for fiscal&nbsp;2005 primarily related to
$89.6&nbsp;million in proceeds received from sales and maturities of marketable
securities net of purchases. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
have made reclassifications to our Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for fiscal&nbsp;2004
and 2003 to reflect the gross purchases and gross sales of dutch auction rate
securities as investing activities rather than as a component of cash and cash
equivalents. Refer to Note&nbsp;2 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements
for additional information.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net cash used in investing activities was $27.5&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004
compared with net cash used in investing activities of $6.7&nbsp;million for
fiscal 2003. Cash used in investing activities for fiscal&nbsp;2004 primarily
related to $19.8&nbsp;million used to purchase support contracts in April&nbsp;2004,
$15.9&nbsp;million used in the acquisitions of Numbercraft, Apexion and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash flows from financing activities</font></i></b>:</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net

in cash received from employee contributions to our employee stock purchase

repurchase of common stock and $1.4&nbsp;million used for repayment of debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net cash used in financing activities was $27.8&nbsp;million for fiscal&nbsp;2004
compared with net cash used in financing activities of $2.8&nbsp;million for
fiscal 2003. Cash used in financing activities reflected $40.0&nbsp;million in
cash used to fund the repurchase of common stock and $0.9&nbsp;million used to
repay debt, which was partially offset by $9.4&nbsp;million in cash provided by
the exercise of stock options, and $3.7&nbsp;million in cash provided by employee
contributions to our employee stock purchase plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h4 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Repurchase of common shares</font></i></b></h4>

<h4 style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></h4>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
June&nbsp;2003, our Board of Directors authorized us to repurchase up to $50.0&nbsp;million
of our common shares. Shares were repurchased as market conditions warranted
either through open market transactions, block purchases, private transactions
or other means. No time limit had been set for the completion of the program. During
fiscal&nbsp;2004, a total of 4.9&nbsp;million shares were repurchased for $40.0&nbsp;million
in cash and $0.1&nbsp;million in non-cash transactions. During fiscal&nbsp;2005
we completed the authorized stock repurchase plan by purchasing 1.4&nbsp;million
shares for $10.0&nbsp;million in cash. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash
proceeds obtained from maturities of marketable securities, the exercise of
employee stock options, and contributions to the employee stock purchase plan
largely funded the share repurchases. The repurchased shares are recorded as
treasury stock and result in a reduction to stockholders equity. The shares
will be used for general corporate purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Contingent cash
commitments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have contingent consideration agreements related to the acquisitions
of Numbercraft in July 2003 and Apexion in October 2003. As of May 31,&nbsp;2005,
additional cash payments ranging from zero to $5.9&nbsp;million are contingent
upon future performance of Numbercraft measured periodically through fiscal
2007 and additional cash payments ranging from zero to $1.0&nbsp;million are
contingent upon the future performance of Apexion measured annually through November
30,&nbsp;2005. Any contingent consideration earned is recorded as additional
goodwill. During fiscal&nbsp;2005 and&nbsp;2004, $0.5&nbsp;million and $1.1&nbsp;million
of additional consideration was earned under the Numbercraft agreement. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2004, we entered into an offshore agreement with a
third-party to provide software maintenance services. If we terminate the
agreement prior to its initial twenty-four month term, a termination fee will
be incurred equal to the sum of the previous six months service charges,
estimated to be approximately $1.6&nbsp;million. At this time, we do not expect
to terminate the agreement within the twenty-four month period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
May&nbsp;9,&nbsp;2005, the Company and International Business Machines
Corporation (&#147;IBM&#148;) entered into a Master Relationship Agreement (&#147;MRA&#148;) and an
OEM Software Agreement, both of which took effect on June&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2005.
Under these agreements, the Company has agreed to standardize its business
applications portfolio on IBM&#146;s open standards-based software and hardware, and
the companies will jointly market these software solutions. Total commitments
under these agreements are in excess of $6&nbsp;million over a 3-year term. The
MRA governs the joint marketing activities and has a three-year term. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
the OEM Software Agreement, we plan to bundle and distribute WebSphere</font>&#174; and
other IBM software products with all of the Company&#146;s business application
products that are designed to operate with these IBM programs. We may
sublicense these IBM programs to &#160;our
current clients in consideration of a sublicense fee payable to IBM. In
consideration of software support provided by IBM&#160; for IBM programs, we have agreed to pay IBM a
portion of support fees paid by our clients.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">If

convenience upon 90 days advance notice to IBM.&#160;
</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;9,&nbsp;2005,
</font>Lawson and Answerthink,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Answerthink&#148;), The Hackett Group,&nbsp;Inc.,
a wholly-owned subsidiary of Answerthink (&#147;Hackett&#148;), entered into an Advisory
Alliance Agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;).&#160;
The Agreement identifies joint programs in which&nbsp;Hackett will
provide Lawson and its clients and prospects with, among other things, access
to&nbsp;Hackett benchmark tools, best practices research and business advisory
services in exchange for the payment of specified program fees. The term of the
Agreement commenced on May&nbsp;9,&nbsp;2005 and continues until May&nbsp;31,
2008 unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of the Agreement.
Lawson and Hackett have the option to extend the terms of the programs upon
mutual written agreement, and Hackett has agreed to provide certain exclusivity
rights to us in connection with certain of its programs. </p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.95pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Agreement,
we have contractually committed to pay Hackett $1.6&nbsp;million. As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,
<br>
$1.1&nbsp;million has been recorded as other accrued liabilities and $0.5&nbsp;million
as other long term liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. We will pay
Hackett additional fees after sales volumes meet established criteria
throughout the term of the contract and will pay an additional $0.5&nbsp;million
in fiscal 2007 if we elect to participate in specified program
initiatives.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We will have additional cash commitments
arising from our pending business combination with Intentia. &#160;If we acquire more than 90%, but fewer than
all of the Intentia securities in
the Exchange Offer, we intend to purchase the remaining Intentia securities for cash, pursuant to compulsory acquisition
proceedings under Swedish law.&#160; Assuming
90% of the Intentia securities are
tendered in the Exchange Offer and the price that is required to be paid
pursuant to the Swedish compulsory acquisition proceedings for the remaining
10% of the Intentia securities equals
SEK 22.17 per Series&nbsp;A share and SEK 19.80 per Series&nbsp;B share, we
could be obligated to pay approximately $48&nbsp;million (approximately SEK 355&nbsp;million
assuming a currency exchange rate of SEK 7.40 to $1.00 as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005),
for the Intentia securities purchased
in the compulsory acquisition. This cash expenditure would normally occur
between one and three years after the closing of the Exchange Offer. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We estimate that the total cash closing
expenses for Lawson and Intentia
will be approximately $15 million, including investment banking fees,
accounting and legal fees, printing, mailing and other out-of-pocket
transaction costs.&#160; After payment of
those expenses, we will have approximately $262&nbsp;million in available cash
and cash equivalents, based on the amount of cash and cash equivalents that we
and Intentia had as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005.&#160;
It is anticipated that we will use an additional amount of approximately
$50&nbsp;million in connection with the transaction, excluding the compulsory
acquisition procedures referenced above and integration related costs, within
one to three years following the closing of the Exchange Offer.&#160; Included in this amount is a junior facility
loan to Tennenbaum valued at $27.4&nbsp;million, which includes accrued
interest of $0.6&nbsp;million, as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005, maturing in September&nbsp;2009,
and a make-whole provision of approximately $9.4&nbsp;million, totaling $36.8&nbsp;million.&#160; Also included in this amount are the
remaining 1999 convertible B notes issued by Intentia valued at $10.1&nbsp;million,
which includes accrued interest of $0.4&nbsp;million, as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our purchase
obligations represent those commitments greater than $50,000.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Under the agreement with Hackett that commenced May&nbsp;9,&nbsp;2005, we
have contractually committed to pay Hackett $1.6&nbsp;million. As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,
$1.1&nbsp;million has been recorded as other accrued liabilities and $0.5&nbsp;million
as other long term liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheet and has been
reflected in the above table. We will pay Hackett additional fees after sales
volumes meet established criteria throughout the term of the contract and will
pay an additional $0.5&nbsp;million in fiscal 2007 if we elect to participate in
specified program initiatives. See
Note&nbsp;15. Commitments and Contingencies to the Consolidated Financial
Statements for additional information.&#160; </p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 33.0pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-33.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On May&nbsp;9,&nbsp;2005, Lawson and
International Business Machines Corporation entered into a Master Relationship
Agreement and OEM Software Agreement, both of which will take effect on June&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2005.
As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005, no amounts have been accrued within the
Consolidated Balance Sheet or included in the above table as the agreement can
be terminated upon 90&nbsp;days notice by either party. Total commitments under
the agreements are in excess of $6&nbsp;million over a 3-year term. See Note&nbsp;15.
Commitments and Contingencies to the Consolidated Financial Statements for
additional information.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 33.0pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-33.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Off-Balance-Sheet Arrangements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
do not use off-balance-sheet arrangements with unconsolidated entities, related
parties or other forms of off-balance-sheet arrangements such as research and
development arrangements. Accordingly, our liquidity and capital resources are
not subject to off-balance-sheet risks from unconsolidated entities. As of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,
we did not have any off-balance-sheet arrangements, as defined in Item
303(a)(4)(ii)&nbsp;of SEC Regulation S-K.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
have entered into operating leases for most U.S. and international sales and
support offices and certain equipment in the normal course of business. These
arrangements are often referred to as a form of off-balance-sheet financing. As
of May 31,&nbsp;2005, we leased facilities and certain equipment under non-cancelable
operating leases expiring between&nbsp;2005 and 2017. Rent expense under
operating leases for fiscal&nbsp;2005,&nbsp;2004 and 2003 was $14.2&nbsp;million,
$14.4&nbsp;million and $16.1&nbsp;million, respectively. Future minimum lease
payments under our operating leases as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005 are detailed above
in &#147;Disclosures about Contractual Obligations and Commercial Commitments&#148;.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004
the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Statement of Financial
Accounting Standard No.&nbsp;123 (revised&nbsp;2004), <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Share-Based Payment (SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R))</font></i>.
SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R) requires compensation cost relating to unvested
share-based payment transactions that are outstanding as of the effective date
and newly issued</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">28</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">transactions to be
recognized in the financial statements. That cost will be measured based on the
fair value of the equity or liability instruments issued. SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R)
covers a wide range of share-based compensation arrangements including share
options, restricted share plans, performance-based awards, share appreciation
rights and employee share purchase plans. SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R) supersedes SFAS No.&nbsp;123,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation </font></i>(SFAS No.&nbsp;123), and supersedes
Accounting Principles Board Opinion No.&nbsp;25, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees </font></i>(Opinion 25)<i><font style="font-style:italic;">.
</font></i>SFAS No.&nbsp;123, as originally issued in 1995, established
a fair-value-based method of accounting for share-based payment transactions
with employees. However, SFAS No.&nbsp;123 permitted entities the option of
continuing to apply the guidance in Opinion 25, as long as the footnotes to
financial statements disclosed what net income would have been had the
fair-value-based method been used. As disclosed in Note&nbsp;2 of Notes to the
Consolidated Financial Statements, we elected the option of disclosure only
under SFAS No.&nbsp;123. In our disclosures, we have historically used the
Black-Scholes option pricing model to determine the fair value of its share
based compensation arrangements. Upon the adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R), we
will determine whether we will continue to utilize the Black-Scholes model or
adopt some other acceptable model. Public entities will be required to apply
SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R) as of the beginning of the first annual reporting period
that begins after June&nbsp;15,&nbsp;2005, which is effective with our first
quarter of fiscal 2007. Based on our significant amount of unvested share-based
payment awards, the adoption of this statement is anticipated to have a
material impact on our Consolidated Statement of Operations, however we are
currently evaluating the impact. Note&nbsp;2 of Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements describes the pro forma impact of a change to fair value accounting
on earnings and earnings per share for the fiscal years ended May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,&nbsp;2004
and 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;153, &#147;Exchanges of
Nonmonetary Assets - An Amendment of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;29&#148; (&#147;SFAS 153&#148;). The
amendments made by SFAS 153 are based on the principle that exchanges of
nonmonetary assets should be measured based on the fair value of the assets
exchanged. Further, the amendments eliminate the narrow exception for
nonmonetary exchanges of similar productive assets and replace it with a
broader exception for exchanges of nonmonetary assets that do not have &#147;commercial
substance.&#148; The provisions in SFAS 153 are effective for nonmonetary asset
exchanges occurring in fiscal periods beginning after June&nbsp;15,&nbsp;2005,
which is effective with our second quarter of fiscal 2006. Adoption of this
standard is not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated
financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:38.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:33.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
May&nbsp;2005, the FASB issued SFAS No 154, &#147;Accounting Changes and Error
Corrections &#150; A replacement of APB Opinion No 20 and FASB Statement No.&nbsp;30&#148;
(&#147;SFAS 154&#148;).&#160; SFAS 154 changes the
requirement for the accounting for and reporting of a change in accounting
principle.&#160; This statement applies to all
voluntary changes in accounting principles and changes required by an
accounting pronouncement in the unusual instance that the pronouncement does
not include specific transition provisions.&#160;
The provisions in SFAS 154 are effective for accounting changes and
correction of errors made in fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15,&nbsp;2005,
which is effective with our first quarter of 2007.&#160; We intend to adopt the disclosure
requirements upon the effective date of the pronouncement.&#160; Since this pronouncement relates to
disclosure only requirements, the adoption will have no impact on our
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

difficulties in integrating our operations, technology and personnel with those

experience integrating operations as substantial and geographically diverse as

operations of Lawson and Intentia in a timely manner, or at all. The failure to
successfully integrate the two companies&#146; operations could undermine the
anticipated benefits and synergies of the combination, which could adversely
affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. The
anticipated benefits relate to greater economies of scale and revenue
enhancement opportunities resulting from Lawson&#146;s and Intentia&#146;s complementary
product offerings, geographic and industry specialties and technology
platforms. However, these anticipated benefits are based on projections and
assumptions, not actual experience, and assume a successful integration.&#160; </font></p>

12 months following closing of the transaction. Our objective is to minimize
incremental costs of operating as a combined company and we believe that any
incremental costs will be offset by cost savings of the combined company. It is
possible that unexpected transaction costs, such as taxes, fees or professional
expenses, or unexpected future operating expenses, such as increased personnel
costs or unexpected severance costs, as well as other types of unanticipated
developments, could adversely impact our business and profitability.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
uncertainties associated with our combination with Intentia may cause our
customers and Intentia&#146;s customers to delay or defer decisions which may result
in the loss of customers and revenues.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our customers and Intentia&#146;s customers may, in
response to the announcement of the Exchange Offer and resulting combination of
Lawson and Intentia, and prior to its effectiveness, delay or defer decisions
concerning business with either or both of the companies. Any delay or deferral
in those decisions by our respective customers could adversely affect our businesses.
For example, either company could experience a decrease in expected revenue as
a consequence of such delays or deferrals.&#160;
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
uncertainties associated with our combination with Intentia may cause Intentia
or us to lose key personnel.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employees of Lawson or Intentia may perceive
uncertainty about their future role with the combined company until strategies
with regard to the combined company are announced or executed. Any uncertainty
may affect either company&#146;s ability to attract and retain key management,
sales, marketing, technical and financial personnel.&#160; </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Combination-related
accounting charges may delay or reduce our profitability.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are accounting for the combination with Intentia as
a purchase following accounting principles generally accepted in the United
States. Under the purchase method of accounting, the purchase price of Intentia
will be allocated to the fair value of the identifiable tangible and intangible
assets and liabilities that we acquire from Intentia. In addition, accounting
for the combination of Intentia under the purchase method may require a
decrease in deferred revenue to fair value. The excess of the purchase price
over Intentia&#146;s tangible net assets will be allocated to goodwill and
intangible assets. We are required to perform periodic impairment tests on
goodwill and certain intangibles to evaluate whether the intangible assets and
goodwill that we acquire from Intentia continue to have fair values that meet
or exceed the amounts recorded on our balance sheet. If the fair values of such
assets decline below their carrying value on our balance sheet, we may be
required to recognize an impairment charge related to such decline. We cannot
predict whether or when there will be an impairment charge, or the amount of
such charge, if any. However, if the charge is significant, it could cause the
market price of our common stock to decline.&#160;
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If as of the
closing date there are unknown liabilities in connection with Intentia&#146;s
business, and those liabilities are not reflected on the closing date balance
sheet, we would be required to record a charge during each period when those
liabilities became known, probable and estimable.&#160; Those charges, if material, could have an unanticipated
and significant adverse effect on our financial results and stock price.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">In
addition, we will incur transaction and integration costs in our combination
with Intentia. &#160;As a result, we will
incur accounting charges from the combination that may delay and reduce our
profitability in the accounting period in which the combination is consummated.
</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
expect to expend a significant amount of cash in the Exchange Offer, which will
partially deplete our cash balance.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If we acquire more than 90%, but fewer than all of the
Intentia securities in the Exchange Offer, we intend to purchase the remaining Intentia
securities for cash, pursuant to compulsory acquisition proceedings under
Swedish law. Assuming 90% of the Intentia securities are tendered in the
Exchange Offer and the price that is required to be paid pursuant to the
Swedish compulsory acquisition proceedings for the remaining 10% of the Intentia
securities equals SEK 22.17 per Series&nbsp;A share and SEK 19.80 per Series&nbsp;B
share, we could be obligated to pay approximately $48&nbsp;million
(approximately SEK 355&nbsp;million assuming a currency exchange rate of SEK
7.40 to $1.00 as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005), for the Intentia securities
purchased in the compulsory acquisition. This cash expenditure would normally
occur between one and three years after the closing of the Exchange Offer.&#160; </font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We estimate that the total cash closing
expenses for Lawson and Intentia will be approximately $15 million, including
investment banking fees, accounting and legal fees, printing, mailing and other
out-of-pocket transaction costs. After payment of those expenses, we will have
approximately $262&nbsp;million in available cash and cash equivalents, based
on the amount of cash and cash equivalents that we and Intentia had as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005.&#160; It is anticipated that we will use an
additional amount of approximately $50&nbsp;million in connection with the
transaction, excluding the compulsory acquisition procedures referenced above
and integration related costs, within one to three years following the closing
of the Exchange Offer.&#160; Included in this
amount is a junior facility loan to Tennenbaum valued at $27.4&nbsp;million,
which includes accrued interest of $0.6&nbsp;million, as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005,
maturing in September&nbsp;2009, and a make-whole provision of approximately
$9.4&nbsp;million, totaling $36.8&nbsp;million.&#160;
Also included in this amount are the remaining 1999 convertible B notes
issued by Intentia valued at $10.1&nbsp;million, which includes accrued
interest of $0.4&nbsp;million, as of May&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Full
integration of our operations with Intentia&#146;s operations may not be achieved if
we cannot compulsorily acquire all of the issued and outstanding Shares.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our obligation to consummate the Exchange Offer is
subject to a condition that, before the end of the Exchange Offer period, there
shall have been validly tendered and not properly withdrawn greater than 90% of
each of the outstanding Shares (including Warrants) and voting power in
Intentia on a fully diluted basis (including all shares issuable pursuant to
outstanding warrants but excluding shares issuable pursuant to outstanding
convertible securities). In addition, the compulsory acquisition proceedings
may be time-consuming.&#160; To effect the
compulsory acquisition under Swedish law, we are required to have a beneficial
interest in greater than 90% of all of the voting power of the Intentia
securities. It is possible that, at the end of the Exchange Offer period, we
will elect to waive the above condition and consummate the Exchange Offer if we
hold at least 70% of the outstanding securities and voting power of Intentia,
even though we do not hold more than 90% of the outstanding Intentia securities.
As a result, we would not be able to effect a compulsory acquisition of the
remaining outstanding securities and voting power of Intentia. This could
prevent or delay us from realizing some or all of the anticipated financial and
strategic benefits of our combination with Intentia.&#160; </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although international revenues accounted for

in staffing and managing foreign operations in Europe and Asia;&#160; </p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>restrictions

accounts receivable collection cycles in Europe and Asia;&#160; </p>

fluctuations and resulting losses on currency translations;&#160; </p>

instability, including inflation and interest rate fluctuations, such as those

for foreign-based suppliers in Asia and Europe;&#160;
</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>overlapping
or differing tax structures;&#160; </p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>cultural
and language differences among the United States, Europe and Asia; and </p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>political

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Any failure on our part to manage these risks
effectively would seriously reduce our competitiveness in the business
applications software marketplace.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As
a result of the consummation of the Exchange Offer, we will be a larger and
broader organization, and if our management is unable to manage the combination
of our business with Intentia&#146;s, our operating results will suffer.&#160; </font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the consummation of the Exchange Offer,
we will acquire the worldwide operations and approximately 2,300 employees of
Intentia. Consequently, we will face challenges inherent in efficiently managing
an increased number of employees over large geographic distances, including the
need to implement appropriate systems, policies, benefits and compliance
programs. Any inability to successfully manage the geographically more diverse
and substantially larger combined organization, or any significant delay in
achieving successful management, could have a material adverse effect on our
results of operations after the Exchange Offer is consummated and, as a result,
on the market price of our common stock. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
new management team might not be able to define or successfully implement a
business plan for the combined companies. </font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2005, we appointed Harry Debes as our new
president, chief executive officer, and director. Upon the completion of the Exchange
Offer, we will appoint a new co-chairman, Romesh Wadhwani, who is currently the
chairman of the board of Intentia, and a new chief operating officer, Bertrand
Sciard, the current president and chief executive officer of Intentia. While Mr.&nbsp;Wadhwani,
Mr.&nbsp;Debes and Mr.&nbsp;Sciard have extensive experience in the software
industry and managing </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">software companies and while Mr.&nbsp;Debes and Mr.&nbsp;Sciard have
also managed large teams of people at other U.S. software companies neither Mr.&nbsp;Debes
nor Mr.&nbsp;Sciard has previously been chief executive or chief operating
officer of a public company in the U.S. If this new management team is unable
to adapt successfully to the demands of managing a U.S. public company or to
define or execute our business plan, our results of operations may be adversely
affected. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Risks Relating to Lawson&#146;s
Business</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
business and company will continue to be subject to other risks and
uncertainties, regardless of whether we complete the proposed business
combination with Intentia.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Economic, political and market conditions
can adversely affect our revenue growth and operating results.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
revenue and profitability depend on the overall demand for computer software,
support and services, particularly in the industries in which we sell our
products and services. Demand for enterprise software and demand for our
solutions are affected by general economic conditions, competition, product
acceptance and technology lifecycles. Regional and global changes in the
economy, governmental budget deficits and political instability in certain
geographic areas have resulted in companies, government agencies and
educational institutions reducing their spending for technology projects
generally and delaying or reconsidering potential purchases of our products and
related services. The uncertainty posed by the long-term effects of the war in
the Middle East, terrorist activities and related uncertainties and risks and
other geopolitical issues may impact the purchasing decisions of current or
potential clients. Because of these factors, we believe the level of demand for
our products and services, and projections of future revenue and operating
results, will continue to be difficult to predict. During fiscal&nbsp;2005 and
the prior three fiscal years, we took measures to realign our projected
expenses with anticipated revenue, and incurred restructuring charges for
severance and related benefits, facility closure or consolidation charges.
There is no assurance that these cost reduction measures will be sufficient to
offset any future revenue declines. Future declines in demand for our products
and/or services could adversely affect our revenues and operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">A number of our competitors are
well-established software companies that have advantages over us.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
face competition from a number of software companies that have advantages over
us due to their larger client bases, greater name recognition, long operating
and product development history, greater international presence and
substantially greater financial, technical and marketing resources. These
competitors include well-established companies such as Oracle Corporation, and
SAP AG, both of which have larger installed client bases. If clients or prospects
want to reduce the number of their software vendors, they may elect to purchase
competing products from Oracle or SAP AG since those larger vendors offer a
wider range of products. Furthermore, Oracle is capable of bundling its
software with its database applications, which underlie a significant portion
of our installed applications. When we compete with Oracle or SAP AG for new
clients, we believe that both of those larger companies often attempt to use
their size and staying power as a competitive advantage against us. Oracle&#146;s
purchase of Peoplesoft,&nbsp;Inc. and Retek Inc., and other consolidations in
the software industry, have fueled uncertainty among client prospects.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
addition, we compete with a variety of more specialized software and services
vendors, including:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Internet
(on demand) software vendors;</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>single-industry
software vendors;</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>emerging
enterprise resource optimization software vendors;</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>human
resource management software vendors;</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>financial

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>merchandising

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>services

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>outsourced
